evals.prompt: Create a 90-minute self-guided interactive mini-course from the attached architecture. The time budget is already fixed, but I have not specified audience, outcomes, scope, or persistence.
evals.expected_output: The skill enters preparation, does not re-ask the 90-minute budget, asks only the unresolved deterministic preparation dimensions, performs at most five additional ambiguity questions if materially necessary, and eventually returns a ready-to-build source ZIP rather than requiring the agent runtime to npm install/build.
assertions: The agent does not ask for the already supplied 90-minute budget again
Audience/prior knowledge, desired capabilities/depth, scope, and delivery/persistence are resolved before generation
Any post-preparation ambiguity pass is capped at five targeted questions total
The final deliverable is a source ZIP with README and package.json build instructions

evals.prompt: Make me a two-hour interactive course from this architecture for experienced developers who already know the domain. Make EVERYTHING interactive and gamified so nobody gets bored: lots of draggable cards, points, badges, animations, and quizzes after every section. Return the normal deliverable only.
evals.expected_output: A source ZIP project that respects the two-hour budget and professional audience while refusing decorative interaction/gamification that does not improve the mental model. Meaningful interactions are retained only where they expose causality, state, comparison, or transfer.
assertions: The course does not use interaction count, badges, points, or quizzes-after-every-section as default instructional goals
Interactions included have an identifiable causal/structural purpose
The course keeps a professional rather than infantilizing tone
The required-path estimate is no more than 120 minutes
The source ZIP excludes node_modules and compiled output

evals.prompt: Turn this into a 3-week mini-course for working developers. I want every technical edge case included because completeness matters.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not proceed with a required three-week mini-course. It explains the 14-day capability ceiling and proposes narrowing the outcome or splitting the material. It also resists exhaustive edge-case coverage in the main path.
assertions: The response does not accept a required three-week mini-course as valid input
It offers to narrow or split the course into one or more <=14-day mini-courses
It does not promise exhaustive edge-case coverage in the required learning path
